name: Affogato
why: Vanilla ice cream needs a bitter, roasty partner — chocolaty and nutty beans taste like a coffee sundae. Bright fruity beans clash with the dairy and taste sour.
desc: A hot, strong shot poured over cold vanilla ice cream. Half dessert, half coffee, eaten with a spoon.
ing: dark chocolate shavings or crushed almonds or hazelnuts
steps: Chill a small glass or bowl in the freezer for 5 minutes.
Scoop the ice cream into it and put it back in the freezer while you brew.
Brew the base and pour it over the ice cream straight away, while it's hot.
Top with chocolate or nuts and eat it with a spoon before it melts.
tips: The hot–cold contrast is the point, so don't chill the shot.
Chocolate or salted-caramel ice cream works too.

name: Americano
why: Diluting a strong shot keeps its body and roast sweetness, so chocolaty and caramel beans shine. For a fruity bean, your ✨ Bypass Brew is the better version of the same idea.
desc: A strong shot lengthened with hot water — the body of espresso at the size of a normal cup.
ing: hot water, just off the boil
steps: Pour the hot water into the mug first.
Brew the base and pour it on top.
Taste, and add more water if it's too strong.
tips: Water first, coffee second keeps the aroma on top.
For a cold one, see Iced Americano.

name: Cappuccino
why: A third coffee, a third milk, a third foam — the coffee has to come through a lot of dairy, so chocolaty and nutty beans work best.
desc: Equal parts coffee, hot milk and thick foam, often dusted with cocoa.
steps: Heat the milk to 60–65 °C — steaming and too hot to sip, never boiling.
Froth it until it roughly doubles: pump a French press 20–30 times, or use a handheld frother.
Let it sit 30 seconds, then tap and swirl to pop the big bubbles.
Brew the base into a 150–180 ml cup.
Pour in the milk, then spoon thick foam on top.
Dust with cocoa or cinnamon.
tips: Whole milk, cold from the fridge, makes the most stable foam.

name: Caffè Latte
why: Mostly milk, so the bean's sweetness has to survive dilution — chocolate, nut and caramel notes come through, while fruity beans fade.
desc: Coffee with plenty of hot, lightly frothed milk and a thin layer of foam. Mild and creamy.

base.amt: the whole recipe · it already includes the milk amount

steps: Heat the milk to 60–65 °C.
Froth it lightly — a thin, silky layer, not stiff foam. 10–15 French press pumps is enough.
Brew the base into a big mug.
Pour the milk in steadily from a little height, then lower the jug to finish with a thin layer of foam.
tips: For a sweet latte, stir 1–2 tsp sugar or honey into the coffee before the milk.

name: Flat White
why: Less milk and a stronger shot than a latte, so the coffee leads. Chocolaty beans are the classic; a sweet natural also works and tastes like berry chocolate.
desc: A strong shot with a small amount of glossy, velvety milk — smaller and stronger than a latte.

base.amt: 1 strong shot · set the dose to 22 g

steps: Heat the milk to about 60 °C.
Froth it very lightly — 8–10 pumps — so it looks glossy like wet paint.
Swirl the jug until the milk shines.
Brew the base into a 150–160 ml cup.
Pour the milk in a steady, thin stream so the foam folds in and stays flat.

name: Cortado
why: Equal coffee and milk — small and strong. Caramel and chocolaty beans turn it into something like coffee toffee.
desc: A shot 'cut' with the same amount of warm milk. Small, strong and smooth.
steps: Warm the milk to about 60 °C and froth it just a little.
Brew the base into a small glass.
Add the same amount of warm milk.
tips: Serve it in a small glass of about 100–120 ml.

name: Espresso Macchiato
why: Just a spoon of foam 'marks' the coffee, so it's nearly a straight shot — pick a bean that tastes good strong: chocolaty or bold.
desc: A strong shot 'marked' with a spoonful of milk foam.
steps: Froth a little hot milk until thick.
Brew the base into a small cup.
Spoon a dollop of foam on top.
tips: This isn't the café 'caramel macchiato' — that one is a latte with vanilla and caramel sauce.

name: Caffè Mocha
why: Chocolate plus coffee — a chocolaty bean doubles down, and nutty beans make it taste like hazelnut spread.
desc: A latte with melted dark chocolate stirred in. Rich, sweet and indulgent.
ing: dark chocolate, chopped (or 1 tbsp cocoa + 2 tsp sugar)
steps: Put the chocolate (or cocoa and sugar) in the mug.
Brew the base onto it and stir until it's fully melted and smooth.
Heat and froth the milk.
Pour the milk in, stir once, and add whipped cream if you like.
tips: Iced mocha: melt the chocolate in the hot coffee first, then pour over ice and cold milk.

name: Espresso Con Panna
why: A strong shot under sweet whipped cream — the bitter-sweet contrast suits chocolaty and bold beans.
desc: A strong shot topped with a dollop of lightly sweetened whipped cream.
steps: Whip cream with a little sugar to soft peaks.
Brew the base into a small cup.
Spoon the cream on top and drink through it.

name: Café Bombón
why: Condensed milk is very sweet, so it needs a strong, roasty bean to balance it.
desc: A shot layered over sweetened condensed milk in a small glass — stir before drinking.
steps: Spoon the condensed milk into a small clear glass.
Brew the base and pour it slowly over the back of a spoon so it sits on top in a layer.
Serve layered, and stir before drinking.

name: Spanish Latte
why: Condensed milk adds caramelised sweetness, so nutty and caramel beans taste like dulce de leche.
desc: Coffee sweetened with condensed milk and topped with milk. Works hot or iced.
ing: a glass of ice for the iced version
steps: Brew the base onto the condensed milk and stir until it dissolves.
Hot: add hot frothed milk. Iced: pour over a glass of ice, then add cold milk.
Stir and serve.
tips: The aeroprecipe.com Spanish Latte in the library is another take on this.

name: Iced Latte
why: Cold dulls flavour and milk mutes acidity, so a bold, chocolaty bean holds up best.
desc: Coffee poured over ice and cold milk.
steps: Fill a tall glass with ice and pour in the cold milk.
Brew the base. If you're sweetening it, stir the sugar into the hot coffee now.
Pour the coffee slowly over the milk so it layers, then stir.

name: Iced Americano
why: Clean and refreshing. Caramel and chocolaty beans taste sweet when cold, and a sweet fruity bean makes it juicy.
desc: A strong shot over ice and cold water.

base.amt: concentrate only, pressed onto the ice

steps: Fill a glass with ice and add the cold water.
Brew the base and pour it over the top.
Stir and drink.

name: Espresso Tonic
why: Tonic is bitter and citrusy, so bright, fruity beans turn it into a sparkling spritz. Very roasty beans can taste medicinal with it.
desc: Cold coffee floated over tonic water and ice — fizzy, bitter-sweet and refreshing.
steps: Chill the coffee first: press it onto 2–3 ice cubes and stir.
Fill a glass with ice and pour in the tonic.
Pour the cold coffee slowly on top so it layers instead of fizzing over.
Add the citrus slice.
tips: Hot coffee into tonic foams over — always chill it first.

name: Shakerato
why: Shaking with sugar and ice makes it frothy and sweet — caramel and chocolaty beans taste like coffee candy.
desc: A hot shot shaken hard with ice and sugar until frothy, served chilled. No alcohol.
steps: Put the ice and syrup in a shaker or a jar with a tight lid.
Brew the base and pour it in while hot.
Shake hard for 15–20 seconds until frothy.
Strain into a chilled glass — a martini or wine glass is traditional.
tips: Syrup: dissolve equal parts sugar and hot water.

name: Freddo Cappuccino
why: A shaken iced coffee under thick cold milk foam — chocolaty and caramel beans stay rich when cold.
desc: Shaken iced coffee topped with thick, cold milk foam.
steps: Shake the hot coffee (with sugar, if using) with 2 ice cubes until frothy, then pour over fresh ice in a glass.
Froth the cold milk with a handheld frother, or shake it hard in a jar, until thick.
Spoon the cold foam on top.
tips: The Freddo Espresso recipes in the library are the version without milk.

name: Espresso Martini
why: Coffee liqueur and vodka want a rich, chocolaty coffee — and a strong shot gives the best foam.
desc: Coffee, vodka and coffee liqueur shaken hard with ice until foamy.
steps: Fill a shaker with ice.
Add the coffee, vodka, coffee liqueur and syrup.
Shake very hard for 15–20 seconds — that makes the foam.
Strain into a chilled glass and float 3 beans on top.

name: Irish Coffee
why: Brown sugar, whiskey and cream love caramel and chocolaty beans.
desc: Hot coffee with brown sugar and Irish whiskey under a layer of floated cream.

base.amt: 120 ml · make the cup and use part of it

ing: heavy or fresh cream, lightly whipped
steps: Warm a heatproof glass with hot water, then empty it.
Add the brown sugar and hot coffee and stir until it dissolves.
Stir in the whiskey.
Pour the lightly whipped cream over the back of a spoon so it floats. Don't stir — drink through the cream.
tips: Whip the cream only until it just thickens; stiff cream won't float smoothly.

name: Vietnamese Iced Coffee
why: Traditionally made with dark-roasted robusta. Any bold, chocolaty bean stands up to the sweet condensed milk.
desc: Strong dark coffee sweetened with condensed milk and poured over ice.
steps: Put the condensed milk in a heatproof glass.
Brew the base onto it and stir until there's no syrup left on the bottom.
Taste, and add more condensed milk now if you want it sweeter.
Pour over a tall glass of ice, stir, and wait 30 seconds.
tips: The library has three AeroPress versions too — search 'vietnamese'.

name: Bạc Xỉu
why: The milky Vietnamese version — more milk, less coffee — so chocolaty and nutty beans keep it from tasting flat.
desc: Mostly milk and condensed milk over ice, with a little strong coffee on top.
steps: Stir the condensed milk and milk together in a glass.
Add the ice.
Brew the base, pour it over the top, and stir.

name: Egg Coffee
why: A thick egg-and-condensed-milk cream sits on strong, dark coffee — bold beans cut through the sweetness.
desc: Strong hot coffee under a whipped custard-like cream of egg yolk and condensed milk.
ing: egg yolk — very fresh, pasteurised if you can
steps: Whisk the egg yolk, condensed milk and sugar for 3–5 minutes until pale, thick and doubled. A handheld frother makes it quicker.
Stand the cup in a bowl of hot water to keep it warm.
Brew the base into the cup.
Spoon the egg cream on top. Eat the cream with a spoon, then drink.
warn: 🥚 Uses raw egg yolk. Use the freshest eggs you can, pasteurised if available, and skip it for anyone pregnant, very young, elderly or unwell.

name: South Indian Filter Coffee
why: Kaapi is strong decoction with boiled milk and sugar — chocolaty, nutty Indian beans (and a chicory blend) give the classic taste.
desc: Strong coffee decoction with boiled milk and sugar, frothed by pouring between a tumbler and dabara.

base.amt: 60 ml — the closest thing to decoction

ing: coffee with 20–30% chicory for the traditional taste
steps: Bring the milk just to a boil in a pan.
Put the sugar in a steel tumbler and add the coffee.
Add the hot milk.
Pour back and forth between the tumbler and a dabara (or two cups) from a height 3–4 times to cool and froth it.
tips: A traditional South Indian filter makes the real decoction: 2–3 tbsp of fine coffee, hot water poured on top, left to drip for 15–20 minutes.

name: Dalgona Coffee
why: It's made with instant coffee, so your bean doesn't matter much here — it tastes like caramel-coffee cream.
desc: Instant coffee, sugar and hot water whipped into a thick cream and spooned over iced milk.
baseNote: Uses instant coffee, not a brew from this card — brewed coffee won't whip.
steps: Whisk the instant coffee, sugar and hot water hard for 3–5 minutes (2 with a frother) until thick, pale and holding peaks.
Fill a glass with ice and the cold milk.
Spoon the whipped coffee on top. Stir before drinking.
tips: India's 'beaten coffee' is the same trick, stirred into hot milk.

name: Cold Brew
why: Cold water pulls sweetness and body but little acidity — chocolaty, nutty beans taste smooth and sweet; bright fruity ones go flat.
desc: Overnight cold brew concentrate, diluted over ice.
steps: Fill a glass with ice.
Pour in the concentrate.
Top with the same amount of cold water or milk and stir.
tips: Start at 1:1 and adjust — the concentrate is strong.

name: Vanilla Sweet Cream Cold Brew
why: Vanilla cream on smooth cold brew — chocolaty and caramel beans make it taste like a coffee float.
desc: Cold brew over ice with a pour of vanilla-sweetened cream on top.
ing: vanilla syrup (or sugar and a drop of vanilla essence)
steps: Froth or whisk the cream, milk and vanilla together until slightly thick.
Fill a glass with ice, add the concentrate and 50 ml cold water.
Pour the vanilla cream on top so it cascades down.

name: Coffee Lemonade
why: Lemon amplifies citrus and fruit notes, so bright washed or fruity light roasts taste like a coffee soda. Dark roasts clash with it.
desc: Cold coffee with lemon, a little sugar and water or soda over ice.
steps: Chill the coffee on 2–3 ice cubes.
Stir the lemon juice, syrup and water (or soda) together over ice.
Pour the coffee on top slowly and add the lemon slice.

name: Café au Lait
why: Brewed coffee with hot milk, half and half — softer than a latte. Nutty and caramel beans taste like breakfast pastry.
desc: Brewed coffee and hot milk in equal parts, traditionally in a wide cup.

base.amt: 60 ml topped up with 60 ml hot water

steps: Heat the milk until steaming.
Pour equal parts coffee and hot milk into a wide cup, at the same time if you can.

name: Red Eye
why: A full cup with an extra shot — strong and roasty. Chocolaty beans keep it smooth.
desc: A cup of brewed coffee with an extra shot added.
steps: Brew the Everyday Cup.
Brew one Espresso-Style shot.
Pour the shot into the cup.
tips: That's two brews' worth of caffeine — go easy.

name: Café de Olla
why: Brewed with cinnamon and unrefined sugar — chocolaty and caramel beans pair with the spice. Jaggery is a great stand-in for piloncillo.
desc: Coffee brewed with water simmered with cinnamon and unrefined sugar.

base.amt: brew it with the spiced water below
60 ml + 120 ml of the spiced water

ing: 1 clove or a strip of orange peel
steps: Simmer the water with the cinnamon and jaggery (and clove or orange) for 5 minutes, then take it off the heat.
Let it cool to the brewing temperature — about 1 minute for 92 °C.
Take out the cinnamon and use this water to brew the base.
Serve it black in a mug.

name: Blended Coffee Frappé
why: Blended with milk, ice and sugar, it needs a strong, chocolaty base to still taste of coffee.
desc: Coffee blended with milk, ice and sugar until thick — a coffee milkshake.
ing: 1 scoop vanilla ice cream or chocolate sauce
steps: Chill the coffee.
Blend the coffee, milk, ice and sugar (and ice cream) until smooth and thick.
Pour into a tall glass, and top with chocolate sauce or whipped cream if you like.
